newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan wants consensus on IMF gold sale proposal.
newsitem.headline: Japan wants consensus on IMF gold sale proposal.

text.p: Japan hopes a consensus will emerge on the International Monetary Fund (IMF) management's controversial proposal to sell off some of its gold to aid the world's poor, a Finance Ministry official said on Thursday.
But the official said it was too early to forecast what progress would be made ahead of an IMF Interim Committee meeting in Washington on September 29.

He said no more formal talks were likely to be held on the issue after an IMF board meeting on Wednesday, but that informal contacts would proceed and that the IMF Interim Committee would discuss the issue and make public the outcome.

IMF management, backed by the United States, Britain, and most other member nations, has proposed selling five million of the fund's 104 million ounces of gold if needed to help finance stepped-up assistance to poor countries.

But a few nations -- Germany, Italy and Switzerland -- have opposed the proposal, saying the IMF should not sell gold except in cases of extreme financial emergency. Some other countries, including France and Japan, have made clear they were unwilling to go ahead with the proposal -- even though they support it -- if that meant isolating those who were opposed, international monetary sources said earlier.
The Japanese official said on Thursday that Tokyo hoped to see a consensus emerge that could be shared by IMF member countries. "We will go along with the consensus," he added.
